prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2017 manifesto (policy-only, ≤500 words)

- Brexit
  - Leave the EU swiftly; restore full parliamentary supremacy and independence from the ECJ, with freedom to choose ECHR membership.
  - Exit the single market and customs union; regain independent WTO seat and trade policy.
  - No “divorce” payment; complete by 2019.
  - Restore a 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone, rebuild fisheries, repeal the 1964 London Fisheries Convention, end discards, require all UK‑caught fish to be landed in the UK, and create a protection force.

- Public finances, tax, cost of living
  - Fund priorities via: cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, cancelling HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with needs‑based allocation, ending EU budget payments, department savings, and NHS cost recovery from ineligible users.
  - No general tax rises; raise the personal allowance to £13,500 and higher‑rate threshold to £55,000; raise inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 (transferable).
  - Abolish the TV licence; remove VAT from domestic energy, hot takeaway food and sanitary products; cut green levies.
  - Crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

- Business and jobs
  - Cut business rates 20% for smaller premises; tackle late payments; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for the self‑employed.
  - Require jobs to be advertised domestically first; protect employment rights; tighten zero‑hours contracts.
  - Coastal enterprise zones with rate relief and housing quality measures.

- Housing
  - Factory‑built modular homes via a Housing Development Corporation on brownfield sites, targeting up to 100,000 a year for under‑40 first‑time buyers; owner‑occupier only, resale back to HDC at cost+inflation. Boost council housing; review housing associations; release dormant public land.

- Health and social care
  - Additional £9bn for the NHS and £2bn for social care by 2021/22; integrate health and social care under one department.
  - Lift medical and nursing training caps; restore nursing/midwifery bursaries; support GP recruitment/returners; add primary‑care support roles.
  - Eligibility: non‑urgent NHS care for citizens or those contributing for 5 years; others require insurance. Improve charge recovery and reciprocity.
  - Regulate NHS managers; limit consultancy spend; abolish hospital parking charges; end new PFIs; Royal Commission on future funding. Guarantee rights for existing EU health and care workers.

- Mental health
  - +£500m per year; 28‑day maximum wait; school counselling and teacher training; enhanced support for armed forces and veterans.

- Education
  - Phonics and core maths focus; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; expand grammar, technical and vocational schools; dual vocational training model.
  - End primary sex education; restore maintenance grants.
  - Abolish tuition fees for STEM and medical degrees with UK service commitments; restrict state loans to courses leading to graduate‑level jobs.
  - Employability/enterprise curriculum; strengthen SEND provision; first‑aid training for all pupils.

- Families and childcare
  - Extend the school day with wrap‑around care; broaden eligible providers; emergency childcare registers; £80m fund to include children with special needs.
  - Presumption of shared parenting; grandparent contact rights; greater family court transparency.

- Older and disabled people
  - Maintain the pension triple lock and existing pensioner benefits.
  - Up to £2bn a year more for social care; improve care worker pay/conditions; ban zero‑hours in home care; pay travel time.
  - £400m a year dementia plan; choice of care at home; reform PIP and Work Capability Assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance; abolish the bedroom tax.

- Migration and integration
  - Reduce net migration to zero over five years via a points‑based and work‑permit system; 5‑year moratorium on low‑skilled migration; seasonal visas; +4,000 border staff.
  - Visa categories (work, study, visit, family) with minimum income for skilled work; five years’ contributions before welfare/non‑urgent NHS; no amnesty; deport foreign offenders.
  - Settled status for law‑abiding EU residents present before Article 50.
  - One law for all; disband parallel religious councils; tougher action on FGM, forced marriage and “honour” crimes; ban face coverings in public; stronger oversight of schools linked to extremism.

- Policing and justice
  - +20,000 police, +7,000 prison officers, +4,000 border staff; restore stop and search.
  - Keep/build prisons; repatriate foreign prisoners; tougher response to prison violence and drugs; curb alcohol‑related disorder via licensing reform.
  - New UK Bill of Rights and leave ECtHR; opt out of the European Arrest Warrant.

- Foreign policy and defence
  - Maintain roles in NATO, UN Security Council, Five Eyes, and the Commonwealth; defend overseas territories; avoid regime‑change wars; retain the nuclear deterrent.
  - Spend a genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus an additional £1bn per year by the end of the parliament; +20,000 personnel; procurement reform.
  - Veterans’ Administration; service card; medal; hostels and housing allocations; guaranteed public‑safety jobs for long‑serving leavers; limit retrospective legal pursuit; income‑tax relief while deployed.

- Trade and aid
  - Shift from aid to trade; reduce aid to 0.2% of GNI and close the standalone aid department; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship; pursue ethical trade with developing nations.

- Transport
  - Scrap HS2; upgrade existing rail and north‑of‑England links; remove road tolls; oppose a third Heathrow runway; support regional airports; freeze then reduce Air Passenger Duty.
  - Expand EV charging; diesel scrappage with no extra penalties; support rural buses; foreign vehicle ID tag.

- Environment, food, energy
  - New Environmental Protection Act; protect ancient woodland; green space and permeable surfaces in developments; address marine plastics; brownfield first; ban pair trawling for sea bass.
  - Replace CAP with a capped UK farm payment favouring active/small, organic and hill farms; support reduced antibiotic use. Animal welfare: ban live export, CCTV in abattoirs, slaughter‑method labelling, tougher cruelty penalties.
  - Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave the Paris Agreement and EU ETS; diversify energy (including shale gas, not in national parks); cut domestic bills by removing VAT and green levies; review utility pricing; end renewable subsidies as contracts expire.

- Democracy and local government
  - Proportional representation; abolish the upper chamber; create an English Parliament; halve the Commons to 325 with PR.
  - Citizens’ initiative with binding biennial referenda; restrict postal voting to need; local binding referenda; cut local waste and keep council tax low.
